1 طَشَّتِ السَّمَآءُ , (S, A, O, K,) aor.
طَشِ3َ and
طَشُ3َ , (O, K,) inf. n. طَشٌّ, (TK,) The sky let fall rain such as is called طَشّ [q. v.]; as also ↓ اطشّت . (S, A, O, K.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] طَشَّ [as meaning (assumed tropical:) He sprinkled the moisture from his nose like fine rain] is said of one affected with the malady termed طُشَّة, when he blows his nose. (O.) ―
-b3- And طُشَّ, (O, K,) with damm, (K,) He (a man) was, or became, affected with the malady termed طُشَّة: (O, K:) but Az says that the [better] known word is طُشِئَ. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
